citation: Guth M. (2022) Predicting Default Probabilities for Stress Tests: A Comparison of Models. arXiv:2202.03110

dedupe_keys.name: comparison of macrofinancial models that predict default probabilities for bank stress tests guth 2022

description: This work compares a large number of regression models that translate macroeconomic variables into default probabilities, the macrofinancial linkage or satellite models at the heart of credit risk stress tests of banks. It sets up a single estimation framework in which many candidate models are estimated and evaluated in the same way, reflecting the need to pick up signals from many macroeconomic variables with short data samples. The results show that some models perform better than the state-of-the-art model then in use, and highlight machine learning models and forecast combinations as promising. It was written by Martin Guth and posted on arXiv on 7 February 2022. Coverage follows the default rate data of the paper, which the abstract does not name. The preprint is available free online; the page read shows only the arXiv licence link, and no code is linked. Caveats: it is a preprint, the data and country are not stated in the abstract, and model rankings depend on the sample used. For simulation it guides the choice of the statistical link between macroeconomic stress scenarios and credit losses in financial stress tests, including those that feed physical or transition climate shocks. It is related to the NUS Credit Research Initiative probability of default record in this catalogue.
